unique.reason: Account stores need-revealing settings against card number with no device-only option; real but modest exposure, since cross-device sync is the stated, expected feature.
Labels repeat unverified vendor claims ("decorative", "for easier reading") and no disabled-reader input is shown; a fair but mostly process-level concern.
Modes are gated on declaring a condition ("I use a screen reader", sr=1, font=dyslexia), which then travels and is stored, turning any leak into direct disability disclosure.
Self-admittedly speculative: material does not say order of transformations or caching; no observed fault to report.
Hard-coded checked defaults and no loading of saved values mean the panel misreports state and one change can silently reset other needed settings.
Visible, spoken reader number aids overhearing/shoulder-surfing; minor, and the material does not confirm it is the card number.
No prefers-reduced-motion or prefers-contrast handling; static defaults ignore OS settings already made. Real, small burden.
Limited range (200% max, two contrast options, vague size names) may not meet some readers' needs; real but a feature-scope limitation.
No reset or delete control and no stated retention for stored need-revealing settings; a real but minor control gap.
Speculative: material gives no basis that service pages are stripped or rewritten, or that caching is misconfigured.
Settings only apply when signed in with the cookie present; sign-in and signed-out pages get defaults. Plausible from material, minor burden.
Removing notes or rewriting likely breaks note references, bookmarks and locations; inferred rather than shown, but follows from the integration text.
Middle-dot separator announcement is negligible and setting-dependent; too trivial to report.
